name: GO Classes Test Series 2024 | Discrete Mathematics | Test 6

question.text: Suppose each person in a group of $4$ friends brings a gift to a party. In how many ways can the $4$ gifts be distributed so that each person receives one gift and no person receives their own gift?

Ten ladies of a certain age drop off their red hats at the hat check of a museum. As they are leaving, the hat check attendant gives the hats back randomly. In how many ways can exactly six of the ladies receive their own hat (and the other four not)?

A permutation $i_1 i_2 \ldots i_n$ of $\{1,2, \ldots, n\}$ is called a derangement if $i_k \neq k$ for any $1 \leq k \leq n$ (no number remains in its position).

The number of derangements of $\{1,2, \ldots, n\}$ is denoted by $\mathrm{D}(n)$. Which of the following is/are true?

  1. Number of derangements $\text{D}(n)$ is odd if the number of items $n$ is even.
  2. Number of derangements $\text{D}(n)$ is even if the number of items $n$ is even.
  3. Number of derangements $\text{D}(n)$ is odd if the number of items $n$ is odd.
  4. Number of derangements $\text{D}(n)$ is even if the number of items $n$ is odd.

A permutation $i_1 i_2 \ldots i_n$ of $\{1,2, \ldots, n\}$ is called a derangement if $i_k \neq k$ for any $1 \leq k \leq n$ (no number remains in its position).

The number of derangements of $\{1,2, \ldots, n\}$ is denoted by $\mathrm{D}(n)$.

How many derangements of $\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}$ have the property that element $1$ is in $5$th place?

GO Classes has five books to review, so we hire five people to review them. We want two reviews per book, so the first week we give each person one book to read and then redistribute the books at the start of the second week. In how many ways can we make these two distributions so that we get two reviews (by different people) of each book?
Let $A=\{1,2,3,4,5\}$. How many injective functions $f: A \rightarrow A$ have the property that for each $x \in A, f(x) \neq x?$

Given any natural number, $n \geq 1,$ let $\text{P}_n$ denote the number of permutations $f:\{1, \ldots, n\} \rightarrow\{1, \ldots, n\}$ that leave no element fixed, that is, such that $f(i) \neq i$, for all $i \in\{1, \ldots, n\}$. Such permutations are sometimes called derangements. Note that $\text{P}_1=0$ and set $\text{P}_0=1$.

Which of the following is/are true for $n\geq 2?$

  1. $
    n !=\text{P}_n+\left(\begin{array}{l}
    n \\
    1
    \end{array}\right) \text{P}_{n-1}+\left(\begin{array}{l}
    n \\
    2
    \end{array}\right) \text{P}_{n-2}+\cdots+\left(\begin{array}{l}
    n \\
    n
    \end{array}\right) $
  2. $\text{P}_n=n !\left(1-\frac{1}{1 !}+\frac{1}{2 !}+\cdots+\frac{(-1)^k}{k !}+\cdots+\frac{(-1)^n}{n !}\right)$
  3. $\text{P}_n= n \text{P}_{n-1}+(-1)^n$
  4. $\text{P}_n=(n-1)\left[\text{P}_{(n-1)}+\text{P}_{(n-2)}\right]$
How many derangements of $\{1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8\}$ begin with the integers $1, 2,$ and $3$ in some order?

The number of permutation of $\{1,2,3,4,5\}$ that keep at least one integer fixed is ___________.

  1. $81$
  2. $76$
  3. $120$
  4. $60$
How many permutations of $\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}$ leave exactly $2$ elements fixed?
How many derangements of $\{1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8\}$ end with the integers $1, 2,$ and $3,$ in some order?

Let $\mathrm{A}=\{1,2,3,4,5\}$. A function $\mathrm{f}: \mathrm{A} \rightarrow \mathrm{A}$ is said to have a fixed point if for some $x$ in $\text{A}, f(x)=x$. How many one-to-one functions $f: \mathrm{A} \rightarrow \mathrm{A}$ have at least one fixed point?
How many ways can the digits $0,1,2,3,4,5$ be arranged so that no even digit is in its original position?

A permutation $i_1 i_2 \ldots i_n$ of $\{1,2, \ldots, n\}$ is called a derangement if $i_k \neq k$ for any $1 \leq k \leq n$ (no number remains in its position).

The number of derangements of $\{1,2, \ldots, n\}$ is denoted by $\text{D}(n)$. How many derangements of $\{1,2,3,4, \ldots, k, \ldots , n\}$ have the property that element $1$ is in $k$th place, and element $k$ is in $1$st place.

It is shown in the diagram below. Assume "$?$" means "Not in this place".

  1. $\mathrm{D}(n)$
  2. $\mathrm{D}(n-1)$
  3. $\mathrm{D}(n-2)$
  4. $\text{D}(n-1)+\text{D}(n-2)$

A permutation $i_1 i_2 \ldots i_n$ of $\{1,2, \ldots, n\}$ is called a derangement if $i_k \neq k$ for any $1 \leq k \leq n$ (no number remains in its position).

The number of derangements of $\{1,2, \ldots, n\}$ is denoted by $\text{D}(n)$.

How many derangements of $\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}$ have the property that element $1$ is Not in the $5$th place?

A permutation $i_1 i_2 \ldots i_n$ of $\{1,2, \ldots, n\}$ is called a derangement if $i_k \neq k$ for any $1 \leq k \leq n$ (no number remains in its position).

The number of derangements of $\{1,2, \ldots, n\}$ is denoted by $\mathrm{D}(n)$.

How many derangements of $\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}$ have the property that element $1$ is in $5$th place, but element $5$ is Not in $1$st place?
Let $\mathrm{A}=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}$. How many injective functions $\mathrm{f}: \mathrm{A} \rightarrow \mathrm{A}$ have the property that for some $x \in \mathrm{A}, \mathrm{f}(x) \neq x?$

The Grinch sneaks into a room with $6$ Christmas presents to $8$ different people. He proceeds to switch the name-labels on the presents. How many ways could he do this if Exactly $7$ presents keep their original labels?

The number of permutations of the characters in $\text{BOTTLE}$ so that no character appears in its original position, if the two $\text{T's}$ are indistinguishable, is  __________.

i.e. Number of Derangements of the word $\text{BOTTLE}?$

Consider $5$ cards, each with a distinct value from the set $\{2,3,4,5,6\}$ and we put them face down to the table. There are $5$ players and Each player is given a number from $2$ to $6,$ no two players have the same number. Each player is given a card by a dealer. A player loses if the value of the given card coincides with the value that player has. If no player loses, then the dealer loses.
How many ways are there so that the dealer loses?
